claims.text: Since 17 Aug 2015 (OAP 2.0, revised as 2.1) USCRN computes 5-minute precipitation as a weighted average of the Geonor's three vibrating-wire depth changes, each wire weighted by its delta variance, with the wetness sensor deciding whether small changes count; no value is computed when the logger door is open, fewer than two wires are valid, or the gauge is over capacity.

evidence.passage: a) Calculate wire weights as a function of the average delta variance

Precipitation is not calculated during maintenance periods. … (less than -15 mm is flagged) … Precipitation is calculated only using wires that pass this check with a minimum of at least two healthy wires remaining. Third, the depth values over the stated capacity of the gauge (either 600 mm or 1000 mm, depending on location) are flagged, and precipitation is not calculated. … Positive depth change values over 25 mm in 5 minutes are flagged automatically … Values can be restored manually using the exception process if found to be real. … wire weights assigned inversely proportional to the delta variance such that noisier wires (more variance) are weighted less. … If the wetness state is yes, the delta for that 5 minutes is retained; if the wetness sensor state is no, the delta is set to zero. If the wetness sensor data are flagged, a more complex approach requiring all three wire deltas to be simultaneously positive and within agreement to 0.5 mm is used … the precipitation must be given in tenths of millimeters, and must exceed 0.2 mm for any 5-minute period.

The existing algorithm for calculating precipitation from the USCRN station configuration was developed by Baker et al. (2005) … The final set of requirements was approved by the USCRN Program Configuration Control Board (CCB) in Configuration Change Request (CCR) 46 on 21 April 2014. The new OAP was documented in a refereed journal publication which was accepted in final form during May 2015 (Leeper et al. 2015a; Appendix 1). … These events are being recorded as exceptions based on procedures adopted by the USCRN Program CCB CCR 42, and are being corrected or flagged as part of the OAP 2.0 project. … A subset of 61 variables is required for precipitation calculation each hour, consisting of values for two wetness sensor channels and three weighing bucket gauge depths for each 5-minute interval, a count of minutes that the data logger door was open during the hour, and the flags for these variables. … all raw inputs to the precipitation calculation have been and will be preserved permanently so that precipitation calculations can be revisited in the future. … the shorthand name for the method was wavgCalc, as the algorithm is based on a weighted average approach to combining the three wire depth change (delta) signals into a single value.
evidence.location: pp.2-4; Appendix 1 = Leeper, Palecki and Davis 2015, J. Atmos. Oceanic Technol., June 2015, pp.1179ff

evidence.passage: 1) Recent revisions to the disdrometer (wetness sensor) range checks inadvertently were not incorporated, which allowed wetness observations that should have been flagged to be used in precipitation calculations; … These events are permanently removed by a manual exception procedure, but the software change limits the size of these events in real time precipitation calculations and prevents 5-minute precipitation values from exceeding established limits. The new version of the precipitation calculation software reflecting this upgrade is referred to as OAP 2.1. … These instances have been well documented and declared to be an exception pending approval by the USCRN configuration control board (CCB). … Port Alsworth, AK, observations were manually flagged using the exception process.
evidence.location: p.2 Introduction; Results and 'Reprocessing Time & Exceptions' sections (text lines 222-301)

evidence.passage: The initial USCRN approach to calculating precipitation from redundant depth observations, pairwise calculation (pairCalc), was found to be sensitive to sensor noise and gauge evaporation. These findings led to … using a weighted average calculation (wavgCalc).
